x: C is correct: Article 46 protects the educational and economic interests of SCs, STs and weaker sections. The others are mismatched: village panchayats are Art. 40 (not 43), cottage industries are Art. 43 (not 40), and prohibition of intoxicating drinks is Art. 47 (not 48).

A is the odd one out: direct court enforcement without legislation is not a criticism, and it is not even true, because Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable. Being not exhaustive (voting, taxes left out), placed as an appendage to Part IV, and vague are all recognised criticisms.

Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the Bill was meant to lift the delimitation freeze and fast-track the 106th Amendment's women's quota, and it failed in the Lok Sabha. Statement 2 is wrong: 298 voted for and 230 against out of 528 present and voting, short of the 352 (two-thirds) needed, so it was not passed.

B is correct: Indra Sawhney (1992) is listed for the principle of equality. Free and fair elections go with Indira Gandhi v. Raj Narain (and Kuldip Nayar), not Minerva Mills; HC powers under Arts. 226-227 with L. Chandra Kumar (1997), not S.R. Bommai; independent judiciary with All India Judges Association and the NJAC case, not Waman Rao.

All three are correct: the SC issued notice (Aug 2026) on a PIL to ban polygamy among Muslims; Javed (2003) held that polygamy is not an essential religious practice; and bigamy is an offence under Sec. 82 BNS.
